options_evaluated: Monomaterial post-consumer recycled (PCR) PC/ABS housing (no overmolded grips)
High-impact polycarbonate (PC) housing with mechanically fastened, replaceable TPU/TPE grips
decisions.conflict: The Material and Circularity agents recommend a monomaterial PCR plastic housing without overmolds to maximize recyclability, whereas the In-Service agent rejects this because a lack of soft grips reduces ergonomics, drop-durability, and tool control.
espr_constraint: Lifecycle principle: material recyclability vs. in-service durability and ergonomics
decisions.chief_resolution: High-impact polycarbonate (PC) housing with mechanically fastened, replaceable TPU/TPE grips. This design ensures necessary ergonomic grip and drop-durability for safe operation while avoiding the inseparable material contamination of overmolding, as the grips can be mechanically detached for recycling.
decisions.design_action: Investigate the supply chain availability of high-impact polycarbonate with certified recycled content and verify mechanical fastening methods for TPU grips.

options_evaluated: Threaded fasteners (screws) with threaded brass inserts
decisions.conflict: The Manufacture agent recommends integral snap-fit joints to simplify production and reduce waste, whereas the In-Service and Circularity agents reject this because snap-fits easily break during disassembly, preventing repair and recycling.
espr_constraint: Lifecycle principle: manufacturing assembly efficiency vs. end-of-life disassembly and repairability
decisions.chief_resolution: Threaded fasteners (screws) with threaded brass inserts. This option facilitates repeated, non-destructive disassembly for maintenance, repair, and component harvesting, which significantly extends the product's useful life.
decisions.design_action: Review standard fastener dimensions to establish a unified screw specification across the housing and internal mounts, and verify compatibility with threaded brass inserts.

options_evaluated: Brushed DC motor with ferrite magnets
Brushless DC (BLDC) motor with easily extractable neodymium (rare-earth) magnets
Coreless DC motor with precious metal brushes
decisions.conflict: The Material and Manufacture agents recommend a brushed DC motor to avoid critical raw materials and reduce production complexity, whereas the In-Service and Circularity agents reject this because brushed motors have lower energy efficiency and a shorter service life.
espr_constraint: Lifecycle principle: upstream material impact vs. use-phase energy efficiency and durability
decisions.chief_resolution: Brushless DC (BLDC) motor with easily extractable neodymium magnets. The use-phase energy savings and vastly superior service life of a brushless motor represent a lower overall environmental impact, provided the motor is designed to allow easy extraction of the rare-earth magnets at end-of-life.
decisions.design_action: Investigate the availability of brushless DC motor suppliers who offer modular rotor designs allowing non-destructive extraction of neodymium magnets.

options_evaluated: Passive cooling via housing ventilation slots and a mechanically secured recycled aluminum heatsink
Active fan cooling with integrated motor fan and removable, cleanable dust filters
decisions.conflict: The In-Service agent recommends active fan cooling with cleanable dust filters to protect the motor under heavy loads, whereas the Circularity and Material agents reject this due to increased material footprint, assembly complexity, and recycling difficulties.
espr_constraint: Lifecycle principle: active thermal performance vs. material minimization and end-of-life recyclability
decisions.chief_resolution: Passive cooling via housing ventilation slots and a mechanically secured recycled aluminum heatsink. This minimizes the bill of materials, avoids the energy consumption of active fans, and ensures the aluminum heatsink can be easily separated and recycled.
decisions.design_action: Investigate the thermal dissipation requirements of the selected motor to verify if passive cooling with a recycled aluminum heatsink is sufficient under continuous load conditions.

options_evaluated: Fully modular architecture with plug-and-play connectors for major sub-assemblies
Semi-modular architecture with soldered wire interconnects
Monolithic integrated design with consolidated components
decisions.conflict: The Manufacture agent recommends a monolithic integrated design to minimize assembly complexity and production waste, whereas the In-Service and Circularity agents reject this because it prevents the replacement of individual failed components, leading to premature tool disposal.
espr_constraint: Lifecycle principle: manufacturing simplicity vs. product repairability and life extension
decisions.chief_resolution: Fully modular architecture with plug-and-play connectors for major sub-assemblies. Enabling the replacement of single failed elements (such as the trigger switch or battery pack) dramatically increases the tool's lifespan, offsetting the initial manufacturing complexity.
decisions.design_action: Investigate standard plug-and-play connector form factors and wire routing requirements to establish a spatial budget for internal modules.

options_evaluated: Standardized, tool-free removable and shareable slide-on Li-ion battery pack
decisions.conflict: The Manufacture agent recommends an integrated Li-ion battery to reduce housing materials and production waste, whereas the In-Service and Circularity agents reject this because it causes the entire tool to be discarded once the battery degrades.
espr_constraint: Lifecycle principle: production resource minimization vs. product longevity and battery recyclability
decisions.chief_resolution: Standardized, tool-free removable and shareable slide-on Li-ion battery pack. A removable battery pack ensures the tool remains functional long after the first battery cycle life degrades, and standardizing the pack across brands reduces the overall number of batteries required by consumers.
decisions.design_action: Investigate existing cross-brand battery alliance standards (such as CAS or Power for All) to determine compatibility requirements for the slide-on interface.
